title: The Drowned Spire
premise: In the salt-locked city of Greyharbor, magic was outlawed a generation ago, and Wren Thornbury has survived by selling harmless charms that are mostly paper and prayer. When the drowned god of the old temple begins answering petitions again, every answered wish leaves the petitioner hollowed — and the trail leads beneath the mountain to a court where souls are currency. Wren discovers her own mother sold her name there years ago to buy the family's survival, and that the last dragon's dying fire is the only thing keeping the court's ledger open. To free herself and the city, she must steal her soul back before the fire gutters out — and in doing so she must choose between exposing the temple elders who built the debt system or preserving the fragile loyalty that holds Greyharbor together. She burns the ledger with the dragon's final flame, freeing thousands of bound souls at the cost of her own memories of her mother, and walks out of the mountain into a city learning to live without debts.
about_author: Paloma Crane is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing maritime folklore along the northern coasts. The Drowned Spire is their second novel, following the acclaimed novella Salt for the Ferryman.

chapters.title: Paper Prayers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. We meet Wren hawking charms in Greyharbor's fish market, dodging the Wardens who enforce the magic ban, while hiding her own small forbidden gift: ink that remembers what it writes. A desperate widow buys a charm and her prayer is actually answered — horribly. Emotional beat: dread disguised as routine; Wren realizes something old has woken.

chapters.title: The Answered Wish
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The widow is found empty-eyed, her memories gone, and Wren's charm is found at the scene. Hunted by both Wardens and the widow's family, Wren flees to the ruined drowned temple where she was indentured as a child scribe. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve as she finds fresh water on the altar — the god is listening again.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Caspian Hale, a disgraced Warden who secretly prays to the old gods. He tracks Wren to the temple but hesitates when he sees the god's sigil glowing in the floodwater. They form an uneasy truce: he wants answers about his brother's 'answered' prayer; she wants to know why hers started this. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of shared guilt.

chapters.title: The Ledger Beneath
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Deciphering her childhood copies of temple records, Wren learns of the Court Below the Mountain, where souls are collateral — and finds her mother's signature on a contract bearing Wren's own name. Her five years of debt-servitude were never random. Emotional beat: betrayal; the ground of her identity cracks open.

chapters.title: Dragonfire, Guttering
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. Guided by smuggler Ossa Vane, they descend through abandoned mine-shafts toward the court, passing veins of stone still warm from a dragon long caged there. The dragon's fire powers the soul-ledger, and it is nearly spent. Emotional beat: awe curdling into urgency — when the fire dies, every bound soul is forfeit, including Wren's.

chapters.title: The Court Below the Mountain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. They reach the court: pale magistrates who trade in names, presided over by the Seneschal, who reveals he negotiated Wren's mother's bargain personally — survival for her daughter's soul. Wren is offered a cruel mercy: walk away and keep her life, forfeit everything else. Emotional beat: temptation of comfortable lies versus unbearable truth.

chapters.title: Loyalty's Weight
chapters.summary: Caspian's POV. Caspian discovers his own brother's soul is in the ledger, sold by Caspian's testimony years ago during his Warden days. The Seneschal offers him restoration of rank if he betrays Wren. He refuses — but Ossa Vane does not, selling their route out to the magistrates. Emotional beat: loyalty tested and broken from within.

chapters.title: The Last Flame
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Captured, Wren is brought before the caged dragon, who speaks in her mother's borrowed voice — the court feeds it memories to keep it burning. It offers her a choice: take its remaining fire and destroy the ledger, but the flame consumes what the bearer loves most. Climax builds. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into willingness.

chapters.title: Ash and Ink
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, climax. Wren uses her remembering-ink to copy the entire ledger onto her own skin, then takes the dragon's fire and burns the original — freeing every bound soul, including Caspian's brother. The flame takes her memories of her mother. The Seneschal, unmade as his contracts void, crumbles. Emotional beat: triumphant sacrifice; the price paid in full.

chapters.title: The City Without Debts
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, resolution. The dragon, freed by the burned ledger, carries them up through the mountain's heart and departs over the sea. Greyharbor reels as thousands wake with their souls returned; the temple elders' debt system collapses, and Wren chooses truth over protection, publishing the records. She mourns a mother she can no longer remember, but the city remembers for her. Emotional beat: bittersweet renewal — inheritance rewritten, survival redefined.
